# hermes-prime

> Two local surfaces deliver one versioned convention card: a reversible,
> marker-anchored Bash injector and a read-only stdio MCP server. Delivery is
> tested; convention adherence and drift reduction are not established.

## What it does

Four subcommands on a single bash binary:

- `--check`: require the fragment file; report companion tools as informational.
- `--print`: print the CLAUDE-fragment to stdout.
- `--inject <project>`: append the fragment to `<project>/CLAUDE.md` between markers; backs up any existing CLAUDE.md.
- `--uninject <project>`: byte-remove an exact injected suffix, remove a file created by injection, or fall back to marker/backup recovery.

Idempotent. Re-running `--inject` is a no-op (size delta ≤ 1 char).

## Install

    git clone https://github.com/hermes-labs-ai/hermes-prime.git
    ln -s "$PWD/hermes-prime/bin/hermes-session-init" /usr/local/bin/hermes-session-init

## What gets injected

A markdown block containing:
- 7 grounding-trigger conditions (when to call hermes-ground)
- Four self-contained conventions (calibration, rubric pass-through, grounding, and name discipline)
- Function-class tool map with Hermes Labs and manual implementations
- The rule most often forgotten mid-session: no noun-phrase label until a file exists at a path.

See `CLAUDE-fragment.md` for the full text.

## When to use

- Starting recursive/emergent work (taxonomy design, rubric construction, structure-discovery debugging).
- Onboarding a fresh `claude --print` subagent that needs the parent session's conventions.
- Restarting a long session in a new context.

## When not to use

- Short single-task sessions where the conventions add noise without payoff.
- Generation-task-only sessions with no grounding or rubric loop.

## Status

Source version `0.2.1-alpha.1` is an unreleased alpha candidate. There is no public
0.2.1-alpha.1 tag or GitHub release, and this source state authorizes neither. The
local acceptance contract is ShellCheck, 11 Bash assertions, 13 MCP tests, and
E2/E3 with byte-identical E3 hashes.

## Related

- hermes-ground — fresh-context grounding agent (the tool the fragment teaches the orchestrator to invoke).
- hermes-rubric — evidence-first scoring; rubric pass-through pattern.
- hermes-blind — a separately invoked multi-turn recovery scaffold.

## About Hermes Labs

Hermes Labs is an agentic infrastructure company building the reliability layer for autonomous systems. This
repository is one bounded convention-delivery mechanism in that portfolio.

Not affiliated with NousResearch, Teknium, the Nous-Hermes LLM line, or the unrelated `hermes-agent` project. Different companies, different work.
